text:
Fraser Minten is scoring like a top-six center, and his name is already showing up in Red Wings trade-target lists (Inside The Rink stacked him up against Detroit's options on Nov. 21). Nine goals in 25 games is a real step for a 22-year-old who came to Boston from Toronto.

Our numbers say some of it is borrowed. He has 9 goals on 5.9 expected (the quality of his chances), he's shooting 18% against 15% last season, and the Bruins have scored 8.5 more goals than expected with him on the ice. That's a lot of luck in one place, and it's why we flag him as due to cool. Boston also gets fewer of the chances with him on than without him at five on five.

What's real: the shot volume is up, his top shot speed sits in the 89th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries last season. Evolving-Hockey valued him at 1.1 wins above replacement then. Watch the finishing settle, and whether the chances keep coming when it does.
